content.text: Davila Carrington and Elaine Cavendish are abducted and driven to a long, low frame building beside Chesapeake Bay, where they are confined in two rooms with barred windows. Their captors treat them courteously, provide meals, and allow a guarded walk outside. The women infer they are being held to force Croyden and Macloud to surrender the supposedly hidden Parmenter jewels. A ransom letter demands $200,000 and threatens them. Elaine offers her own certified check, sending a note to the Tuscarora Trust Company in Northumberland. The women are then moved from the house aboard a tug in the Bay. Meanwhile, Croyden and Macloud organize payment, notify detectives, and agree to avoid rescue attempts. Macloud travels to New York to obtain cash, returns to Annapolis, and Croyden rides across the Severn toward Greenberry Point to deliver it.
